meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (federal-state hybrid constitutional system; Alberta is a common law jurisdiction)

Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and regulations thereunder, administered by FINTRAC; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2 (proceeds of crime); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 23; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2. Provincial: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), including Alberta corporate transparency reforms requiring private corporations, including unlimited liability corporations, to maintain an internal Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register accessible to the Director of Corporate Registries, FINTRAC and other prescribed authorities; the Alberta register is not publicly searchable.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Service Alberta Corporate Registry (via accredited NUANS search house)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued directly to the applicant; no notarization or apostille required for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and proof of residential address of each UBO / individual shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or commissioner for oaths in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if originating in a Hague Convention member state, e.g., United States) or Consular Legalization at the relevant foreign consulate/embassy in Canada for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and certified constitutive documents of any corporate shareholder (e.g., United States LLC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent foreign companies registry (e.g., Secretary of State in the United States)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization chain, including notarization and certification by the competent authority of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Office Consent and Acceptance Form (registered office service provider)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic document; no notarization or apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all directors, officers, UBOs and authorized signatories against foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs) per PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance 7G; mandatory screening against the OFAC SDN List and OFAC sectoral sanctions (US nexus required for USD payment rails and US securities filings), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the consolidated Canadian autonomous sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Criminal Code and the United Nations Act; screening must be completed before director/UBO approval, refreshed within 90 days of any ownership or control change, and documented in the corporate KYC file for disclosure to banking counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – online corporate registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin/Roman alphabet; the registered legal name must contain a distinctive element and a descriptive element followed by the mandatory legal element for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation: 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Corporation'; names in English or French are accepted, while non-Latin scripts, diacritical marks and symbols are not permitted in the registered legal name; a minimum three-character distinctive element is required; any parallel brand in a non-Latin script must be protected separately as a trade-mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant receives the Registrar's written refusal with the grounds. The applicant may, within 30 days of refusal, submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Corporate Registries, Service Alberta, attaching a fresh NUANS report and supplementary evidence (e.g., consent letters from professional bodies, registered trade-mark certificates, or customary-name affidavits from the applicable industry). If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative review request and may ultimately seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta. Concurrently, the applicant may file a new name reservation under a different distinctive element. Unused name reservations lapse automatically upon expiry of the 90-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for this digital-app issuer. The ABCA requires a registered office at a real, physical street address in Alberta (not a post office box) where service of process and statutory notices can be delivered; a commercial virtual office or registered-office services arrangement with an Alberta-based provider satisfies this requirement. A physical storefront, local employees or in-province operations are not required for an ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 software and app publisher.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk of approximately 5% over the first 24 months. Service Alberta and FINTRAC primarily conduct documentary and electronically lodged compliance reviews rather than unannounced on-site premises inspections. The probability rises to approximately 15–20% if the corporation triggers tax or AML red flags, allows the registered office to lapse, elects non-resident directors without UBO documentation, or becomes a U.S. reporting issuer subject to CRA/FINTRAC correspondence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 12(1)(b) (unlimited liability corporation designation), 15(1) (Articles of Incorporation), 101-102 (registered office), 105 (first directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction), acting through authorized Corporate Registry Agents for online filings
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 3, ULC variant) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; shares may be issued for nominal consideration; no escrow or capital deposit account required in Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: (1) The incorporation of the Corporation as an unlimited liability corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) is ratified and approved. (2) The registered office is adopted at [registered address], Alberta, and the Corporate Secretary is authorized to file any notice of change. (3) The directors named in the Articles of Incorporation are confirmed, and the issuance of 1,000 common shares at CAD 1.00 per share to the initial subscriber is approved. (4) [Name] is appointed President, and [Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, each to serve until successors are duly elected. (5) The corporate seal and specimen share certificate are adopted, and the officers are authorized to open and operate banking accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure NUANS Corporate Name Search Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an authorized Corporate Registry Agent (NUANS online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an authorized Alberta Corporate Registry service provider to conduct a NUANS search against federal, Alberta, and other Canadian corporate names and registered trademarks. Select a distinctive name carrying the mandatory legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC', and obtain the preliminary search report prior to filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and up to three alternatives
Brief description of the health-fitness software business activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name collides with an existing mark, promptly select the next cleared alternative or obtain a written letter of consent from the interfering party; a fresh NUANS search is then required at the standard fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute ULC Articles of Incorporation (Form 3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and corporate legal counsel under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 3 Articles of Incorporation in the ULC format containing an express statement that the corporation exercises unlimited liability under s. 12(1)(b) ABCA. Set out the share structure (unlimited common shares), first directors, and the full Alberta registered office street address, and have each incorporator execute the articles together with consents to act.
required_dossiers: Form 3 Articles of Incorporation with ULC statement
Consent to Act as First Director (Form 27)
Registered office street address in Alberta (no post office box)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting deficiencies such as a missing ULC statement or incomplete director consents and re-execute before submission; no additional government fee is incurred if corrected prior to filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deliver Articles and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (online filing portal or authorized Registry Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Form 3 articles through the secure registry portal or an authorized agent and pay the statutory filing fee. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon satisfactory review; the effective date is the date of filing, at which point the ULC acquires legal personality with all statutory corporate powers.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership information collected at filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of deficiency, respond within the stated deadline (generally 30 days) with amended articles; a rejected application is refunded less one-half of the filing fee, and re-filing requires a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for CRA Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, access the CRA Business Registration Online system to obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN). Register for GST/HST if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 per year, register for payroll deductions if employees will be hired, and activate the Alberta corporate income tax account, which is administered by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act coordination agreement.
required_dossiers: Alberta registry attachment showing ULC designation
Board authorization for CRA access and bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the ULC status, provide the Certificate of Incorporation and the articles showing the s. 12(1)(b) unlimited liability clause; tax registrations are generally made effective as of the date the application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Business Licence and Premises Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal business licensing office (City of Calgary or City of Edmonton); Safety Codes Act fire authority; Alberta Workers' Compensation Board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the ULC leases an office, development studio, or data-center space, apply to the relevant municipal business licensing office for a general business licence. Secure fire and life-safety clearance under the Alberta Fire Code, and register with the WCB before any employees commence work. Ensure leased premises meet the workstation and ergonomics requirements of the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal licence objections are cured by supplementing the lease and fire evacuation documentation; a licence refusal may be appealed to the Subdivision and Development Appeal Board within 21 days, and WCB coverage is retroactive to the hire date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Board Meeting and Establish Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to formalize governance: adopt corporate by-laws, ratify the registered office, issue initial common shares, approve the share register and minute book, appoint banking signatories, and set the annual corporate maintenance calendar. File the Alberta annual return within 60 days after the anniversary month and confirm beneficial ownership through the Corporate Registry Portal.
required_dossiers: Adopted first board resolution (minutes or written resolution)
Executed share certificates and share register
Minute book with registers of directors, officers, and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is filed late, pay the late-filing fee and file immediately; persistent non-filing beyond two consecutive years triggers a notice of dissolution risk, which may be cured by a rectification filing with the Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 digital software operations are not subject to any industrial or manufacturing licence in Alberta; general municipal business licensing for office premises is the only physical-location requirement.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the health-fitness app software product; an optional general business licence is issued by the City of Calgary or City of Edmonton for office-based operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - zero-discharge software and office operations; no EIA registration or report required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-3, Schedule 1; no approval under the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous wastes are generated by the software business; applicable obligations are limited to municipal wastewater and solid-waste bylaws, e-waste diversion under the Alberta Recycling Regulation (A.R. 18/2004), and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 for disposal of electronic equipment; biometric health data is governed by PIPEDA and Alberta PIPA rather than environmental law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and life-safety certificate under the Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Act, SA 2000, c S-1) for leased commercial premises; OHS ergonomic and workstation clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code for computer-based staff; structural load inspections are required only if the lease premises are physically modified; a WCB account is mandatory once employees are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA/ARC), with business registration portal 'My Business Account' and Business Registration Online (BRO); certain provincial corporate registration and tax filings with Alberta Corporate Registry and Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration are coordinated through CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishes an Alberta ULC via incorporation or extra-provincial registration with Alberta Corporate Registry. It must then obtain a CRA Business Number (BN), which serves as the statutory TIN, and any program accounts (RT for GST/HST, RC for payroll, RP for non-resident taxes, RD for customs). Applications are made through BRO or by filing Form RC1/RC186 with the CRA (or by using the Alberta Online Incorporation service which transmits initial BN data). Required supporting information includes the certificates of incorporation, registered office address, names of directors/officers, Canadian mailing address or representative, and estimated revenue; for non-residents, a valid non-resident corporation account may be opened and a section 150(2)(A) treaty waiver assessed where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Canadian federal or Alberta election allows a ULC to be taxed as a partnership or sole proprietorship; it remains a corporation subject to Part I corporate tax and Alberta corporate income tax. Cross-border owners may however elect under U.S. check-the-box rules (IRS Form 8832) to treat the ULC as disregarded or partnership for U.S. tax, and the Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty's hybrid-entity provisions may modify treaty eligibility. Canada has no election to be treated as a tax-exempt zone entity or an Investment Trust. Hybrid mismatch elections are generally not available domestically.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), Harmonized Sales Tax where applicable; Alberta does not impose a provincial sales tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (taxable supplies made in Canada, including 'specified supplies' of digital intangibles/services to Canadian recipients, in a current calendar quarter or in the last four consecutive calendar quarters; registration becomes mandatory once the threshold is met).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time tax clearance, digital stamping, or CRA invoice pre-approval. Electronic invoices with digital signatures are recognized. Registered businesses must report through GST/HST NETFILE or EDI and retain full point-of-sale/API transaction logs. CRA online services provide the GST/HST program account remittance API and create/update digital registration information; non-resident digital suppliers use the simplified GST/HST registration portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply of an exported good is zero-rated under Part V Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act, if the supplier maintains satisfactory evidence that the goods were exported. For intangible personal property like a fitness/health app or biometric tracker data, a supply to a non-resident person is zero-rated when the supply does not require the supplier to enjoy/consume the property in Canada, is not in connection with Canadian property/services, and is not made to a Canadian resident. The app's exportation of digital telemetry must be supported by contracts, platform download/use records, non-resident client evidence and payment flows. Pure digital subscriptions sold to non-residents may qualify for zero-rating when the place of supply is outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A / Canadian Export Reporting System proof) or CBSA acknowledgment for goods
Commercial invoice and signed sales agreement / digital supply contract
Export bill of lading / air waybill / shipper's export declaration
Evidence of foreign payment and inward remittance certificate / bank SWIFT confirmation
Non-resident registration and place-of-supply evidence (IP address country logs, foreign billing address, app-store country storefront records)
CRA GST/HST zero-rated export substantiation schedule (internal reconciliation of invoices to export evidence)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess any zero-rated supply as taxable (GST/HST at 5% plus provincial component where applicable) if documentary proof is missing, payment does not originate from a non-resident, or the app is found to be used in Canada. Civil gross-negligence penalties of 50% of understated net tax can be imposed along with a false-statement penalty of 25% of the net tax evaded (minimum CAD 5,000), and criminal sanctions exist for intentional evasion. Retrospective reassessment generally covers four years from the filing date, but extends to ten years where there is misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange policy and oversight are jointly administered through the Federal Department of Finance (policy lead), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI, prudential supervision of financial institutions), and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC, AML/CFT transaction reporting), all operating under the Bank of Canada Act, the Currency Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada maintains no dedicated central foreign-exchange-control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible with an open capital account. Current-account items (subscription revenue from Apple IAP / Google Play, licensing fees, cloud compute outflows) are freely convertible without prior approval. Capital-account transactions (shareholder capital injections, intercompany loans, dividends, repatriation of proceeds) are unrestricted with respect to conversion and remittance, subject only to: (i) Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents (statutory 25%, generally reduced to 5%–15% under the Canada–US Tax Treaty for a corporate shareholder of an Alberta ULC); (ii) CRS/FATCA reporting; and (iii) FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) obligations for transactions exceeding CAD $10,000. No in-Canada retention ratio, no prior-exchange-approval requirement, and no profit-remittance licence apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory remittance timeline for export or digital-services revenue. Export proceeds and app-store settlement funds may be retained in any currency and any jurisdiction at the exporter's discretion. Compliance obligations are limited to: (i) FINTRAC reporting by the Canadian bank for incoming/outgoing EFTs of CAD $10,000 or more; (ii) record retention for six years under subsection 230(a) of the Canadian Income Tax Act; and (iii) transfer-pricing documentation under Section 247 of the Income Tax Act for transactions with non-resident related parties such as a US parent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (primary USD correspondence via TD Bank US)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ATB Financial (Alberta Treasury Branches, provincial Crown corporation)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (provincial treasury alignment, CAD clearing only)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, subject to strict conditions. Canada does not recognise European EMI licences; foreign digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) may be used only as ancillary payout rails and cannot serve as the primary clearing bank for a Canadian ULC. A Canadian-domiciled fintech provider must register with FINTRAC as a Money Service Business (MSB) and, if covered, as a Payment Service Provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) administered by the Bank of Canada. Use of any foreign EMI requires that the ULC maintain its primary liquidity and capital-escrow accounts at a Schedule I domestic bank, and that the EMI's Canadian MSB registration be verified on the FINTRAC registry before onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for Canadian-resident signatories at most Schedule I banks through video KYC, but for a ULC with non-resident directors or beneficial owners, at least one director, officer, or authorised agent with signing authority must attend an initial in-person account-opening interview at a physical Alberta branch when expected annual commercial throughput exceeds CAD $250,000 or when non-resident capital contributions exceed CAD $1,000,000. A 90-day physical-verification condition is standard: the bank sends a compliance officer or a designated notary to verify the ULC's Alberta business substance. Fully remote opening without any physical touchpoint is generally not available for capital-escrow accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) resident in a high-intensity or non-EEA jurisdiction, or a negative-news hit on the beneficial owner's name triggering Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport/photo ID and proof of residential address; notarised source-of-wealth statement; bank reference letter from the originating institution; corporate registry extracts for every entity in the ownership chain; a sworn explanation of the transaction trail supporting the capital injection; and, where applicable, a clean regulatory background check from the jurisdiction of residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office matches a law-firm or registered-agent address with no evidenced Alberta business substance, creating a pass-through or shell-company risk flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Alberta commercial lease or co-working membership agreement; CRA payroll account confirmation with Alberta-resident employees; Alberta Operations Manager declaration detailing daily treasury and product-development functions; and Alberta Corporate Registry Certificate of Status confirming active standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-profile mismatch: retail consumer subscription revenue (Apple IAP / Google Play, CAD $10–$30 per month) versus large cross-border software-licensing and cloud-infrastructure disbursements, triggering a suspicion of trade-based money laundering or tax-evasion structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console revenue dashboards for the trailing 12 months; cloud-provider invoices (AWS/Azure/GCP) matching the disbursement ledger; a rolling 13-week cash-flow treasury model explaining each clearing-rail route; and executed intercompany agreements with the US parent for IP licensing and cost-recovery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Alberta ULC's US check-the-box pass-through tax classification creates an ambiguous beneficial-ownership chain, and the bank requests proof of Canadian tax filing and Part XIII withholding clearance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canadian legal opinion confirming the ULC is a resident corporation under the Income Tax Act; Alberta registry 'Certificate of Status'; executed shareholders' agreement; applicable W-8BEN-E/W-8BEN forms; most recent T2 corporate income tax return (or nil-filing acknowledgment); and a written undertaking to remit Part XIII withholding tax on all future non-resident dividend payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for US/foreign parent funding to the ULC's Schedule I bank account in Calgary: (i) SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAPL' (capital contribution) or explicit narrative 'Capital Contribution – Shares issued under the Alberta Business Corporations Act'; (ii) include the ULC's full legal name, account number, and the originator's Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) where available; (iii) the bank files a FINTRAC EFTR for any wire of CAD $10,000 or more; (iv) for share issuance in exchange for property, file Form T2057 (if applicable) and retain the directors' resolution authorising the capital call; (v) for inbound non-cash property, obtain an independent valuation and record fair market value in the ULC's financial statements; (vi) for wires exceeding USD $10,000 from a foreign corporate parent, be prepared to evidence the substance and business rationale under OSFI Guideline E-12, including a copy of the investment agreement and the ULC's funding plan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for IP licence fees, cloud-infrastructure payments, intercompany service charges, and non-resident dividends (with Part XIII withholding applied); (2) commercial letters of credit (sight or term) for any physical infrastructure or capital-equipment procurement, issued through the same Schedule I bank; (3) domestic CAD wholesale payments above CAD $100,000 cleared via Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS); (4) sub-CAD-$100,000 payments cleared via the real-time rail (RTR) where available, or through standard EFT; (5) USD-denominated outflows netted through the bank's US correspondent (e.g., TD Bank US or RBC Bank, Georgia) for same-day settlement; (6) app-store settlement receivables (Apple IAP / Google Play) arrive via ACH, SEPA, or global EFT into the operational account with a daily automated sweep into an interest-bearing operational reserve to maximise liquidity yield.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD outright forward contracts (tenors up to 12 months) executed through a Schedule I bank dealing desk
CAD/USD cross-currency swaps (deliverable, for long-dated capital-structure hedging)
Plain-vanilla over-the-counter CAD/USD currency options (calls and puts)

FX forwards embedded in commercial risk-participation agreements with OSFI-regulated counterparties; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not applicable to CAD/USD and are reserved only for non-convertible emerging-market currency exposures, subject to OSFI/CSA derivatives trade-reporting obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return and Good Standing Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Government of Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of the anniversary date of incorporation in each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative late fees as prescribed in the corporate registry fee regulations; continuing default for three consecutive annual periods can trigger administrative dissolution under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, with reinstatement normally requiring court intervention or Director's approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta Corporate Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the ULC's taxation year-end; for a calendar-year ULC, the return is due by June 30 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month, up to a maximum of 12 months; CRA may impose collection measures or require the return by formal demand. This filing does not trigger Alberta registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a non-reporting Alberta ULC, no revenue or asset threshold alone compels an audit. An audit is mandatory unless all shareholders unanimously consent, each year, to waive the appointment of an auditor under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. Any shareholder request for an auditor, public distribution of securities, or reporting-issuer status makes the audit compulsory. The contemplated privately held fitness-app ULC can normally rely on the unanimous-consent waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook, for a non-publicly accountable Canadian private corporation; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) would apply only if the ULC becomes a reporting issuer or if shareholders require publicly accountable financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Alberta Annual Return is filed by a director or officer and confirms the registered office and current directors. Separately, the ULC must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) and update it within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control. Before filing the annual return, the ULC should review and finalize the ISC register; any new 25% or more shareholding or control change must be reflected prior to the annual confirmation. No separate provincial UBO filing fee applies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – USD 450 per year for a standard Alberta registered-office and registered-agent service.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 – USD 10,000 per year if a full independent audit is required; reduced review engagement may be appropriate if the unanimous-consent waiver is not available and shareholders accept a review.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (filed via CRA's E-filing / NETFILE for corporations, or using certified tax software; GST/HST and provincial administration integrated)
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the corporation's taxation year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end is due by June 30); instalments of Part I tax are due monthly (or quarterly if the corporation is an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation)
